help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Since then Mr Klein saves every file in the cloud as well.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Zum Glück introduces the rescue: something goes right after the problem.
help.tips[0].en.text: Find the three parts: what went wrong (der Bildschirm blieb schwarz), how it was fixed (Zum Glück …), what he does now (Seitdem …). Each part carries at least one question.
help.tips[0].en.title: Problem → solution → lesson
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Luckily he had also sent the file by e-mail to his colleague Ms Brandt the evening before.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: His presentation was saved on the hard drive, but the device would not start any more.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: war abgefahren is the Plusquamperfekt: it looks one step further back than ankamen.
help.tips[1].en.text: hatte … geschickt happened the evening before the story’s morning — and it is the key to the rescue. When a narrative in the Präteritum switches to hatte / war + participle, it is looking further back.
help.tips[1].en.title: Plusquamperfekt = the step before the story
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The next day the computer was collected.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: There they told him that the computer could be repaired the next day at the earliest.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: The passive tells you what happened and leaves out who did it.
help.tips[2].en.text: wurde geöffnet, wurde abgeholt: the text does not say by whom, because it does not matter. Questions about these sentences ask what happened, not who did it.
help.tips[2].en.title: The passive hides who did it
help.hookEn: Follow a small office disaster from black screen to rescue, and learn to spot what went wrong, what saved the day and what changed.
help.introEn: A short narrative of about 200 words about a mishap — Herr Klein’s computer dies on the morning of his presentation — told in the Präteritum, with one step further back in the Plusquamperfekt (hatte … geschickt), several passives (wurde geöffnet, wurde abgeholt, repariert werden konnte) and a since-then in the present (Seitdem speichert er …). Blog posts and stories like this are everyday reading, and you read them for what happened, how it was solved and what changed. The six questions follow the narrative: the problem, what customer service said, the rescue, the talk, the next day and the lesson. The technology vocabulary from earlier in the module comes back in context — einschalten, Bildschirm, Festplatte, gespeichert, Gerät, Datei, Kundendienst.
help.rememberEn[0]: Past for what happened, hatte + participle for what came before, present after seitdem for what changed.
help.examEn: Short personal narratives like this blog post are a standard reading text in the B1 exam.
